Chapter 2 · Tips 11–20

People, Process, and Productivity

人、流程与生产力

Save Money on Your Issues在问题上省下钱

Randy Loomis, PMP · Andover, Connecticut, U.S.Randy Loomis（PMP）· 美国康涅狄格州安多弗

OUR COMPANY WAS USING TRAINING SOFTWARE that was five upgrades behind. We reached the point where it was so out of date that the vendor would no longer support it. Our project consisted of working with the vendor to upgrade our training software to the latest release, and then to train our users to use the newest version.

我们公司用的培训软件落后了五个大版本。最后老到供应商都不再提供支持了。我们的项目就是和供应商合作，把培训软件升级到最新版本，然后培训用户使用新版。

We developed two statements of work, one that outlined the user training agreement and one that delineated a "not-to-exceed" cost for applying the upgrades to our old training software. After obtaining a copy of our data, the vendor began the process of remotely developing and testing the scripts necessary to begin converting the data and applying the first of the upgrades.

我们拟了两份工作说明书：一份写用户培训协议，另一份写明对旧培训软件做升级的"不超过"成本上限。供应商拿到我们的数据副本后，开始远程开发并测试脚本，用于数据转换和打第一个升级包。

* Script: In computer programming, a program or sequence of instructions carried out by a program rather than the computer processor. Scripts can control a software application without altering its core code.* 脚本：在编程中，由程序而非计算机处理器执行的程序或指令序列。脚本可以在不改动应用核心代码的情况下控制软件应用。

Once the scripts passed vendor testing, they were migrated to our development environment where we performed user tests. This process was repeated as we added each of the five subsequent upgrades. While doing testing, we would document any issues that we encountered, then we retested those issues once the vendor had rewritten and retested their original scripts.

脚本通过供应商测试后，迁移到我们的开发环境做用户测试。后续五个升级包，每个都重复这个流程。测试时，我们把遇到的问题记录下来，等供应商改写并重新测试完原始脚本后，再回归测试这些问题。

— p.48 —

While working through each of the upgrades, the vendor's hours, multiplied by the billing rate established in the statement of work, were tracked against the "not-to-exceed" budget. As we progressed through the upgrades, we discovered bugs in the application upgrades themselves that were not related to the custom scripts written to install the upgrades. We thoroughly documented each issue, printing screens and providing step-by-step details of what we discovered, and how and where we encountered each issue.

在做每个升级时，供应商的工时乘以工作说明书里的计费单价，对照"不超过"预算进行跟踪。随着升级推进，我们在应用升级包本身发现了一些 bug，与为安装升级而写的自定义脚本无关。我们把每个问题都详细记录下来：截屏、逐步描述发现了什么、在什么情况下、在哪里遇到的。

We also brought the vendor proof showing what we had originally been promised the software would do. The vendor insisted that the software was functioning "as designed." Later, we discovered that the small bugs we had encountered were only the tip of the iceberg and had greater ramifications. They illuminated significant problems with the software's basic functionality, even after the upgrades.

我们还拿出证据，向供应商展示当初承诺软件该做什么。供应商坚称软件是"按设计"运行的。后来我们发现，遇到的那些小 bug 只是冰山一角，背后影响更大。它们暴露出软件基本功能在升级后仍存在的严重问题。

Over time, the vendor conceded that several of the issues we discovered were admittedly not "as designed"; rather, they were actual bugs. Remaining true to our "not-to-exceed" contract, our vendor did not charge us for the significant amount of work they were required to do to correct their own product after they reached the "not-to-exceed" total in our contract.

久而久之，供应商承认我们发现的几个问题确实不是"按设计"，而是真 bug。按"不超过"合同约定，供应商在达到合同总额后，修复自家产品所需的大量工作不再向我们收费。

At this stage of the project, in order to meet critical deadlines, we were completely focused on getting the software installed. Our concern of whether an issue was "as designed" or a bug was the least of our worries. It became apparent that, had we been tracking vendor time specifically against each bug issue located, we might have avoided paying the "not-to-exceed" contract total cost.

在项目这个阶段，为了赶关键截止日，我们一门心思把软件装上。某个问题到底是"按设计"还是 bug，已经顾不上计较。事后才看明白：如果当初把供应商的工时按每个 bug 分别记账，我们也许根本不必付满"不超过"合同的总价。

When negotiating a contract with a vendor, specify that both the vendor's and your project team's time be tracked against each separate issue that is encountered. This will allow the software project manager to have an accurate record and be able to lower charges when there are issues with the vendor's original product, as opposed to problems with the contractual project work to implement it.

和供应商谈判合同时，要写明：供应商和你方团队的工时，都按遇到的每个独立问题分别记账。这样软件项目经理就有准确记录，当问题出在供应商原始产品上（而非合同约定的实施工作上）时，就能相应降低费用。

— p.49 —

How to Spot a Good IT Developer如何识别优秀的 IT 开发

James Graham, PMP · Ta' l-Ibrag, MaltaJames Graham（PMP）· 马耳他

SOFTWARE PROJECT MANAGERS know that project success rests on having excellent developers. How do you spot stellar performers in the applicant herd?

软件项目经理都知道，项目成功靠的是优秀的开发人员。怎样在一大群应聘者中识别出拔尖的人？

Before new candidates interview, talk to your best developers. Have them reaffirm the specific knowledge needed. Is experience with a particular development life cycle, a specific methodology, special toolsets, or definitive sector knowledge (experience in the defense industry or the pharmaceutical sector, for example) preferable, or mandatory?

在新候选人面试之前，先和你最优秀的开发聊一聊，让他们确认岗位到底需要哪些具体知识。是偏好、还是必须具备：某个特定开发生命周期的经验？某种方法论？特定工具集？还是明确的行业知识（比如国防或制药行业经验）？

Assess knowledge. Mix interviews, involving you and trusted representatives from your development team, with theoretical tests. A good software engineer will be able to fix "mock" syntax errors immediately and without any mental stress. He or she can read other people's code and understand its intent without extensive documentation or glyph-by-glyph translation. When presented with a programming problem, your candidate should be able to spot it and then describe it in both "developer geek" and in language appropriate for non-information technology stakeholders.

评估知识。把你与开发团队可信赖代表参与的面试，和理论测试结合起来。好的软件工程师能立刻、毫无心理压力地修复"模拟"语法错误。他/她能读懂别人的代码，不必靠大量文档或逐字翻译就能理解意图。面对一个编程问题时，候选人应当能先指出问题，然后用"开发者黑话"和非 IT 利益相关者能听懂的语言分别描述它。

We all think "more is better" when hiring programming skills. But how do we define "more"? Although a candidate may have excellent knowledge, this person may not yet have developed the finesse to employ it effectively. A recent graduate or newly trained developer may struggle to apply the theoretical knowledge gained in an educational context when facing a demanding real-world project. When tight deadlines squeeze the time to explore solutions, and intense pressures from the client and other stakeholders loom, you need experience on top of raw knowledge.

招人时我们都觉得"越多越好"。但怎么定义"多"？一个候选人知识渊博，却未必练就了有效运用这些知识的手感。应届毕业生或刚受训的开发，面对苛刻的真实项目时，可能难以把课堂上学到的理论知识用出来。当紧巴巴的工期压缩了探索方案的时间，当客户和其他相关方的巨大压力压过来时，你需要的是在知识之上的经验。

Ask the applicant/developer to write code for review by you and your team. After analyzing the code and talking with your trusted developers, you will sense whether this person's approach and style will fit your team.

让应聘者现场写一段代码，供你和团队评审。分析代码、和你信任的开发聊过之后，你就能感觉出这个人的思路和风格是否适合你的团队。

— p.50 —

Consider the candidate's attitude toward work, coworkers, clients, and stakeholders. I once worked with a developer known as "The Hair Dryer." Legend has it that when he was upset, he could blow people's hair dry with his shouting. He was an excellent developer, but a detriment to a project team.

还要考察候选人对工作、同事、客户和相关方的态度。我曾经共事过一个外号叫"吹风机"的开发。传说他一发火，吼一嗓子就能把别人的头发吹干。他是个优秀的开发，但对项目团队却是个害。

As the world moves toward agile development methodologies, cross-functional communication and soft skills will increase in importance. Developers will find themselves working in small teams with people from elsewhere in the organization. How well will your potential new teammate represent you when unleashed into the wild? Follow these simple guidelines when hiring software developers:

随着业界走向敏捷开发方法论，跨职能沟通和软技能的重要性会越来越高。开发会发现自己在小团队里，和来自组织其他部门的人一起工作。你这位未来的新队友被放出去之后，能在多大程度上代表你？招软件开发时，请遵循这些简单准则：

  • Screen them to check for the right knowledge of development life cycles, methodologies, toolsets, and their industry/sector familiarity.
    筛选：考察他们对开发生命周期、方法论、工具集的知识，以及对所在行业/领域的熟悉度。
  • Test them to see a demonstration of their ability to apply their knowledge in your workplace.
    测试：让他们示范在你的工作环境中运用知识的能力。
  • Check out their communication and social skills.
    考察沟通和社交能力。
  • Look for the right attitude toward the work: a balance of desire to create high-grade products while accepting the project constraints. Is there documented evidence that they can produce products that are "fit for purpose," on time, and within the budget?
    看对待工作的态度：既渴望做出高质量产品，又能接受项目约束。是否有书面证据表明他们能按时、按预算交付「合用」的产品？

No matter how personable and skilled your applicant, always verify credentials with the issuing institutions and check out resume entries with former employers. Careful hiring practices may prevent a multitude of future problems.

无论应聘者多招人喜欢、多有本事，都要向发证机构核实证书，并向以前的雇主核对简历。谨慎的招聘能防住一大堆未来的麻烦。

— p.51 —

Developer Productivity: Skilled Versus Average开发效能：高手与普通的差距

Neal Ford · Atlanta, Georgia, U.S.Neal Ford · 美国佐治亚州亚特兰大

LET'S DEBUNK SOME OF THE MYTHS about developer skills for project managers who have been assigned for the first time to software projects. Understand that really good software developers are much more productive than average ones. In fact, some statistics say that really good developers are multiple orders of magnitude better than poor ones. One order of magnitude is the same as multiplying a quantity by 10. The point is, a skilled programmer isn't just a little better than an average one; the difference is huge.

为初次接手软件项目的项目经理，破除几个关于开发技能的迷思。请明白：真正优秀的软件开发者，效能远高于普通开发者。事实上，有统计说高手与差手之间差着好几个数量级。一个数量级就是乘以 10。重点是：熟练程序员不是比普通程序员好一点，而是好得惊人。

What should this mean to our newly minted software project managers as they plan the development of this product? Managers erroneously think that even if you can't get the best and brightest, you still get some usefulness out of mediocre developers. But building software isn't like digging a ditch, where even the poorest ditch diggers can make a hole.

新上任的软件项目经理在规划产品开发时，该怎么理解这件事？经理们错误地认为，就算招不到最聪明的人，平庸的开发也能出点活。但造软件不是挖沟——最差的挖沟工也能挖出一个坑。

In software development, what is programmed today becomes the foundation for tomorrow. If you have mediocre developers building your foundation, the really good developers have to go back and fix the flaws before they can move on. Hiring mediocre or average developers slows project velocity. Frequently, taking a poor performer off the team is more beneficial than adding a good one.

在软件开发中，今天写的代码就是明天的地基。如果让平庸的人打地基，高手们就不得不回头先修补缺陷，才能继续前进。招平庸或普通的开发会拖慢项目速率。很多时候，把一个差手移出团队，比加一个好手进来还有益。

* Velocity: In agile software development, the rate of progress of a team or team member—how much an individual programmer can produce in a given time period.* 速率（Velocity）：敏捷软件开发中团队或团队成员的进展速度，即一个程序员在给定时间内能产出多少。

Couple this with the fact that adding people to a late project makes it even later, and you can understand why most enterprise development moves at a glacial pace. The nonexperienced software project manager might reason that if adding more warehouse men allows a truck to be loaded faster, hiring additional programmers would shorten the time necessary to complete a software project.

再加上"给已经延期的项目加人只会让它更延期"这一事实，你就能理解为什么大多数企业开发慢如蜗牛。没经验的软件项目经理可能会类推：既然多几个仓库工能更快装满一辆卡车，那多招几个程序员不也能缩短软件项目工期吗？

— p.52 —

That won't work. It will take time, and pull other programmers off-task, to get the new guys/gals up-to-date. In addition, the communication channels increase with each addition to the team. With a team of two, there is one channel: Betsy Sue to Bill. Add Mike, and you jump to three channels. The number of channels continues to grow exponentially. Here's the formula: n(n–1)/2. With 12 people on the team, you have 12(12–1)/2 channels, or 66 relationships you must maintain as the project manager. Add one more person, and you now have 78 communication channels to oversee.

这套不管用。让新人上手需要时间，还会把其他程序员从手头任务里拽出来。而且，团队每加一个人，沟通渠道就增加。两个人的团队只有一条渠道：Betsy Sue 到 Bill。加个 Mike，跳到三条。渠道数呈指数增长。公式是 n(n–1)/2。团队 12 人时，你作为项目经理要维护 12×11/2 = 66 条关系。再加一个人，就要管 78 条沟通渠道。

Building software with average developers exposes two project myths: 1) that you can shorten a project by adding people, and 2) that it's OK to have average developers produce average (buggy/off-task) code at an average pace. In truth, average developers drag overall productivity down and the project takes longer than necessary to complete.

用普通开发造软件，暴露了两个项目迷思：1）加人能缩短项目；2）让普通开发以普通节奏写出普通（带 bug、跑偏的）代码也没关系。事实是，普通开发会拉低整体效能，项目完成时间比必要的更长。

The solution? Give good developers powerful tools. You'll get higher-quality software faster. Second, having warm bodies doesn't help projects, and having to babysit poor developers cuts the productivity of your good developers, who are craftsmen. Software is too complex to turn into an assembly-line manufacturing process.

解法是什么？给好开发配强大的工具。你会更快拿到更高质量的软件。其次，多几个凑数的人对项目没帮助，而照看差手还会拖累你那些手艺人——好开发的产能。软件太复杂，没法变成流水线制造。

Want faster software development? Spend the extra money to hire and nurture excellent software developers. It will pay off in both the short term, and in the long term when it's time to maintain the code.

想让软件开发更快？多花点钱，招并培养优秀的软件开发者。短期有回报，长期维护代码时更有回报。

— p.53 —

Size Matters规模很重要

Anupam Kundu · New York, New York, U.S.Anupam Kundu · 美国纽约州纽约市

THE SIZE OF THE PROJECT, the size of the team, the size of the deliverables, and the size of the checklists—everything in a project depends on its SIZE. Size changes the rules of how the game is played.

项目的规模、团队的规模、交付物的规模、清单的规模——项目里的一切都取决于它的"规模"。规模一变，游戏规则就变。

The bigger the project gets (in size or complexity), the more important it becomes for a project manager to break down the project into manageable modules and share the delivery responsibility of these modules with capable people. This will ensure that key project members, including the project manager, can see the "big picture" without getting lost in the details while scouting for project health statistics.

项目越大（规模或复杂度越高），项目经理就越需要把项目拆成可管理的模块，并把这些模块的交付责任分担给能干的人。这样才能保证包括项目经理在内的关键成员，在查看项目健康指标时既能看到"大局"，又不迷失在细节里。

Distributed projects tend to be bigger in size than other project types; hence, the tactics the project manager uses to manage the size actually impacts the bottom line of the project. The word "big" conjures up a variety of images. It can mean anything from eight people working for 12 months (if you are a small vendor) to hundreds of people working on annual maintenance contracts (if you are an enormous IT partner for your client).

分布式项目往往比其他类型规模更大；因此，项目经理用来管理规模的策略，会实实在在影响项目的盈亏底线。"大"这个词能唤起各种画面。它可以指 8 个人干 12 个月（如果你是小供应商），也可以指几百人做年度维护合同（如果你是客户的巨型 IT 合作伙伴）。

Here are a few suggestions on how to carve out the right size for the project and then make sure that everyone understands how the small parts of the puzzle can make or break the big picture:

以下是几点建议，帮你为项目切出合适的规模，并让每个人明白：这一小块拼图如何成就或毁掉大局：

  • Break down the project into as many independent, yet manageable, workstreams as possible.
    把项目拆成尽可能多、相互独立又可管理的工作流。
  • Make sure each workstream has at least one key contact point responsible for its delivery.
    确保每个工作流至少有一个关键接口人，对其交付负责。
  • If possible, try to have key members play overlapping roles in these workstreams so that the "big picture" is shared across the teams.
    如果可能，让关键成员在多个工作流中兼任角色，使「大局」在团队间共享。
  • Track the progress (use any tool) of each workstream separately, and tie up the metrics at regular intervals to feel the pulse of the overall project.
    用任意工具单独跟踪每个工作流的进度，定期汇总指标，把握整个项目的脉搏。
  • Document and share the risks, issues, assumptions, and dependencies of each workstream separately.
    分别记录并共享每个工作流的风险、问题、假设和依赖。
  • Organize regular team meetings to share the status of each and every workstream.
    定期组织团队会议，分享每个工作流的状态。
  • Publish an overall project roadmap, including release plans from all different workstreams.
    发布整体项目路线图，包含所有工作流的发布计划。
  • Use online tools aggressively to share user requirements, milestone updates, bug reports, report timelines, and risks.
    积极使用在线工具共享用户需求、里程碑更新、bug 报告、报告时间线和风险。
— p.54 —

For example, imagine you are entrusted with building three versions of the same website (North America, Asia-Pacific, and Mid-East). You decide it is best to create three different workstreams, each with an independent delivery contact person. Since all three sites are basically the same sites in a different version (leading to medium customization), have a few key resources float across all three workstreams. This way, they can ensure the overall integrity of the sites and suggest reuse of implementation details.

举例：设想你受托为同一个网站建三个版本（北美、亚太、中东）。你决定最好建三个不同的工作流，每个有独立的交付接口人。既然三个站点基本是同一站点的不同版本（中等定制），就让几个关键资源在三个工作流之间浮动。这样他们能保证站点的整体一致性，并建议复用实现细节。

Another example might be that you have multiple integration vendors for a single project. It might be ideal to separate out each integration point (or a related collection of them) into an individual workstream. This will allow simultaneous channels of work and may shorten the delivery time. Involve the different teams in daily meetings to coordinate the overall quality of the delivery.

另一个例子：一个项目有多个集成供应商。把每个集成点（或一组相关集成点）单独拆成一个工作流，可能是最理想的。这样可以并行作业，缩短交付时间。让不同团队参加每日站会，协调交付的整体质量。

— p.55 —

Document Your Process, Then Make Sure It Is Followed把流程写下来，然后确保被遵守

Monte Davis, MCSE · Omaha, Nebraska, U.S.Monte Davis（MCSE）· 美国内布拉斯加州奥马哈

DURING AN EMAIL MIGRATION FROM ONE PLATFORM TO ANOTHER, a woman got married and brought our email system to its knees.

在一次邮件系统从一个平台迁移到另一个平台的过程中，一位女士结了婚，结果把我们的邮件系统搞瘫了。

The email flow works like this: 1. New emails coming in are delivered through the new email system. 2. If the new email system can, it delivers the message to the appropriate new system user. If not, the message is sent on to the old email system for delivery. 3. Emails sent from someone still on the old system to someone still on the old system are delivered to the appropriate mailbox. However, if the recipient has already been migrated to the new system, the email is automatically forwarded using a "migration" forwarding address created for each user.

邮件流转是这样的：1）新进来的邮件先经过新邮件系统投递。2）新系统能投递的，就投给对应的新系统用户；不能的，就转给旧邮件系统投递。3）旧系统用户发给旧系统用户的邮件，投到对应邮箱。但如果收件人已经迁到新系统，邮件会通过为每个用户创建的"迁移"转发地址自动转发。

Here's where the funny part comes in. Once Sally Single was migrated to the new email system, she had two email addresses, sally.single@mycompany.com, as well as a forwarding email address, sally.single@migrate.mycompany.com. All email sent to her from users on the old system would automatically be forwarded to the new mail system using her "migration" forwarding address.

好玩的部分来了。Sally Single 迁到新邮件系统后，有两个地址：sally.single@mycompany.com，以及一个转发地址 sally.single@migrate.mycompany.com。旧系统用户发给她的邮件，都会通过这个"迁移"转发地址自动转到新邮件系统。

When Sally got married and changed her name from "Sally Single" to "Sally Married," her email address changed as well. However, the person who renamed Sally's email address in the new system forgot to change her email "migration" forwarding address on the old system. So, Sally ended up with the following addresses.

Sally 结婚后，名字从"Sally Single"改成"Sally Married"，她的邮箱地址也跟着改了。但是，在新系统里给她改名的那个人，忘了改旧系统上她的"迁移"转发地址。于是 Sally 的地址最后变成这样：

New SystemOld System
1. sally.married@mycompany.com1. sally.married@mycompany.com
2. sally.single@mycompany.com2. sally.single@mycompany.com
3. sally.married@migrate.mycompany.com3. sally.single@migrate.mycompany.com
(婚礼后被忽略的、未改动的原始迁移条目)
— p.56 —

When emails were sent to Sally from users still on the old messaging system, they created a loop: 1) Messages were created and sent on the old mail system to sally.single@mycompany.com; 2) old mail system checks Sally's account and sees that forwarding is set to sally.single@migrate.mycompany.com and forwards the messages; 3) the new mail system looks for someone with an email address equal to sally.single@migrate.mycompany.com, but it doesn't find it, since that address was renamed when Sally got married, so 4) the new mail system forwards the messages for the unknown recipient back to the old mail system; 5) the old mail system knows to forward all messages with an @migrate.mycompany.com address, so it forwards them to the new mail server; and 6) lather, rinse, repeat.

当旧系统用户给 Sally 发邮件时，就形成了一个死循环：1）旧邮件系统生成邮件发到 sally.single@mycompany.com；2）旧系统查 Sally 的账户，发现转发设到 sally.single@migrate.mycompany.com，于是转发；3）新邮件系统找地址等于 sally.single@migrate.mycompany.com 的人，但找不到——因为这个地址在 Sally 结婚时被改名了；4）新系统把这个"未知收件人"的邮件退回旧系统；5）旧系统知道所有 @migrate.mycompany.com 的邮件都要转发，于是又转给新邮件服务器；6）打泡、冲洗、重复。

Every time the messages loop, the corporate legal disclaimer is added to the end of the messages. The legal disclaimer is only about 100 words, but when each message is looping between systems several times a minute, this adds up quickly. Evidently, Sally was very popular. There were so many messages sent to Sally that the size and volume of the messages brought the mail system to a grinding halt.

邮件每循环一次，末尾就被加上公司的法律免责声明。免责声明才 100 来字，但当每分钟每封邮件在两个系统之间循环好几圈时，量很快就堆起来了。显然，Sally 非常受欢迎——发给她的邮件多到把整个邮件系统挤停摆。

Moral of this story: document your processes and make sure the process is followed. Although the name change process had been documented, it was not being followed. Otherwise, Sally's user account on the old mail server would have been updated with her new, married name migration email address, and the issue would have been avoided.

这个故事的寓意：把流程写下来，然后确保流程被遵守。改名流程虽然写下来了，却没被执行。否则旧邮件服务器上 Sally 的账户就会更新成她婚后的新迁移邮箱地址，这个问题本来可以避免。

— p.57 —

Go Ahead, Throw That Practice Out尽管把那个做法扔掉

Naresh Jain · Malad, Mumbai, IndiaNaresh Jain · 印度孟买

WHAT DO SUCCESSFUL TEAMS DO THAT OTHERS DON'T? They constantly question their own practices and try to eliminate wasteful ones. They mercilessly refactor their processes along with their software.

成功的团队做了哪些别人不做的事？他们不断质疑自己的做法，努力淘汰浪费的做法。他们像重构软件一样，无情地重构自己的流程。

Il semble que la perfection soit atteinte non quand il n'y a plus rien à ajouter, mais quand il n'y a plus rien à retrancher. This French quote from Antoine de Saint Exupéry means "Perfection is attained, not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away.

Antoine de Saint Exupéry 有句法语名言："完美不是无可添加之时，而是无可删减之时。

Why don't teams apply this principle today? Why is it that over a period of time, the value of the end product gets thinner and thinner, and the process and byproducts get bulkier and bulkier? Why do the lines of code expand, while the useful features of the software become fewer and fewer?

为什么今天的团队不践行这条原则？为什么随着时间推移，最终产品的价值越来越薄，而流程和副产品却越来越臃肿？为什么代码行数膨胀，软件的有用功能却越来越少？

Key indicators that things are "broken" in the software development processes:

软件开发流程"坏掉"的关键信号：

  • The software bloats up in terms of lines of code and useless features.
    软件在代码行数和无用功能上膨胀。
  • The team building the software keeps growing in size.
    造软件的团队规模不断扩大。
  • The process gets more and more prescriptive, dogmatic, and rigid.
    流程越来越规定化、教条化、僵化。
  • The team is experiencing "death by planning" meetings.
    团队正在经历「被计划会议压死」。
  • The amount of documents and supporting artifacts increases exponentially.
    文档和配套制品数量指数级增长。
  • Newly discovered bugs keep pouring in from customer test groups.
    客户测试组不断冒出新发现的 bug。

Team leaders have a tendency to keep adding more processes, more checks, and more audits, thinking that an increasingly stringent process will solve the problem. In my experience, it's never a process issue. Adding more processes will only make it that much more difficult for the team to see the root cause of the real problem.

团队负责人倾向于不断加流程、加检查、加审计，以为越来越严格的流程能解决问题。以我的经验，问题从来不在流程。加更多流程，只会让团队更难看清真正问题的根因。

— p.58 —

Why is it that most teams are afraid to throw away practices that are not really helping the team? Why do teams start off with as many practices they can think of, instead of adding the practices just in time?

为什么大多数团队不敢扔掉那些其实没什么用的做法？为什么团队一开始就把能想到的做法全堆上，而不是及时按需添加？

This could be a symptom of the team not really understanding why it is using the process in the first place. Or it could mean that someone who does not fully understand the software development process is forcing a heavy-handed methodology upon the team. In either case, the project becomes a "house of cards" ready to disintegrate into a useless pile of code bits. Trying to change anything, without understanding the true reason the project is expanding without adding value, is useless.

这可能说明团队根本没理解自己当初为什么用这个流程。也可能意味着某个并不真正理解软件开发流程的人，正把一套沉重的方法论强加到团队头上。无论哪种情况，项目都变成了"纸牌屋"，随时会塌成一堆没用的代码碎片。如果不理解项目为何在不增加价值的情况下膨胀，任何改变都是徒劳。

In my opinion, a good project manager should have a healthy grasp of how the team is working. He/she should be able to stand back and evaluate how each process imposed on the team impacts the throughput of functional software. A knowledgeable project manager should sift through all the possible activities a team might be asked to do and retain only those that are vital to the success of this specific project. Once the leftover practices from projects past are swept away, the team's productivity and throughput should get better in a short period of time.

在我看来，好的项目经理应当清楚团队是怎么工作的。他/她应当能退一步，评估强加给团队的每个流程对"可用软件产出量"的影响。有见识的项目经理会筛掉团队可能被要求做的各种活动，只保留对这个特定项目成功至关重要的那些。一旦把过去项目遗留的做法清扫干净，团队的产能和产出会在短时间内好转。

The phrase "less is more" is a very important philosophy when it comes to process.

谈到流程，「少即是多」是一条非常重要的哲学。

— p.59 —

Requirement Specifications: An Oxymoron需求规格：一个矛盾修饰

Alan Greenblatt · Sudbury, Massachusetts, U.S.Alan Greenblatt · 美国马萨诸塞州萨德伯里

GOOD REQUIREMENTS (R) describe how features of a product are going to solve particular existing or potential problems. Good features (F), sometimes called functionality, are added to products to address those important problems. Requirements are captured by salespeople or created by software project managers:

好的需求（R）描述产品功能将如何解决特定的现有或潜在问题。好的功能（F，有时叫功能性）是为解决这些重要问题而加到产品上的。需求由销售人员收集，或由软件项目经理制定：

  • We can't sell the product outside of the United States (R). We need to provide internationalization and localization support (F).
    我们的产品无法卖到美国以外（R）。我们需要提供国际化和本地化支持（F）。
  • Users have to click five buttons to complete a very simple task. They get frustrated and never complete the task. We need to simplify the user interface (R) and reduce the number of button clicks to two or fewer to complete the same tasks (F).
    用户要点击五个按钮才能完成一个非常简单的任务。他们感到挫败，再也不完成这个任务。我们需要简化用户界面（R），把完成同一任务的点击次数减到两次或更少（F）。

Specifications (S), on the other hand, describe exactly how problems will be solved and the requirements will be met. Using the examples above, the following specifications might be written by systems architects:

而规格说明（S）则精确描述问题将如何解决、需求将如何满足。沿用上面的例子，系统架构师可能写出如下规格说明：

  • We will extract all text strings, including pop-up messages, and place them in external resource bundles (S).
    我们将提取所有文本字符串（含弹出消息），放入外部资源包（S）。
  • The application will be enhanced so that all text displayed on the screen will be retrieved from these resource bundles (S).
    改造应用，使屏幕上显示的所有文本都从这些资源包读取（S）。
  • Localization can be performed by creating specific resource bundles for the locales required (S).
    本地化通过为所需区域创建专门的资源包来完成（S）。
  • The functionality achieved through clicking buttons 1, 2, and 3 will be bundled into a single button click on Button A (S).
    把按钮 1、2、3 点击所实现的功能，合并到按钮 A 的一次点击中（S）。
  • The functionality of existing buttons 4 and 5 will be bundled into Button B (S).
    把现有按钮 4、5 的功能合并到按钮 B（S）。
— p.60 —

Blurring the lines between requirements and specifications leads to the wrong people making the decisions. You either end up with the software developers making decisions about what features are important to a user, or with a software project manager telling a developer how to structure code. Either way, the result is a poor final software product.

把需求和规格说明的界限搅浑，会导致错误的人做决策。最后要么是软件开发人员来决定哪些功能对用户重要，要么是软件项目经理来指挥开发怎么组织代码。无论哪种，最终软件产品都很差。

Developers aren't usually out talking to customers, users, marketing, sales, and potential partners, trying to understand what new features are most important. On the other hand, software project managers usually aren't skilled developers who understand how best to implement a feature, and how their untrained, although well-meaning, specification suggestions would affect other aspects of the product. Each group has a unique skill set.

开发通常不在外面跑，不和客户、用户、市场、销售、潜在伙伴交流，去理解哪些新功能最重要。反过来，软件项目经理通常不是熟练的开发，不懂得怎样最好地实现一个功能，也不明白自己那番未经训练、虽出于善意的规格建议会怎样影响产品的其他方面。两边各有独特的技能组合。

Having good requirements that describe the problem you are trying to solve, and why it is so important to solve this particular problem, lets the programmer be more flexible, efficient, and motivated during the development process. Coders can make independent design decisions as they work on the problem and understand it more thoroughly. They should only be bound by the technologies they have chosen to use, not by strict, brittle specifications created by a nonprogrammer.

有了好的需求——描述你要解决的问题，以及为什么解决这个问题如此重要——程序员在开发过程中会更灵活、更高效、更有动力。编码者在解决问题、深入理解问题时，可以独立做设计决策。他们只应受自己选择采用的技术约束，而不应被非程序员写出的、死板脆弱的规格说明绑住手脚。

Specifications still need to be written, but they will change. Have you come to the end of the product development cycle and only then fully understood how this product should have been built in the first place?

规格说明还是要写，但它一定会变。你是不是也有过这样的经历：走到产品开发周期的尽头，才完全明白这个产品当初到底该怎么建？

Keep the what you are trying to build separate from the how to build it. Then, let the properly trained team member make decisions based on his/her project role.

把"要造什么"和"怎么造"分开。然后，让受过相应训练的团队成员，根据自己的项目角色做决策。

— p.61 —

Success Is Always Measured in Business Value成功永远以业务价值衡量

Barbee Davis, MA, PHR, PMP · Omaha, Nebraska, U.S.Barbee Davis（MA, PHR, PMP）· 美国内布拉斯加州奥马哈

AS PROJECT MANAGERS, it's easy to get caught up in meeting our time, cost, scope, and quality baselines. The project quickly becomes an end in itself, and our personal worth becomes entwined with our ability to bring this project in according to these measurable expectations.

作为项目经理，我们很容易陷在满足进度、成本、范围、质量基线里。项目很快变成了目的本身，我们的个人价值也和"能否按这些可衡量的期望把项目做完"绑在了一起。

We need to focus on the fact that the project is only as successful as the business value it adds to the organization. If we're producing a software product for market, the evaluation factors for "success" are clear. We need to use our project management skills to bring this product to market quicker so we can get it sold to a large portion of the customer base before the competition is able to produce a similar or even better product.

我们必须聚焦于一个事实：项目有多成功，取决于它给组织增加了多少业务价值。如果我们做的是面向市场的软件产品，"成功"的评价标准很清楚：我们要用项目管理技能把产品更快推向市场，赶在竞争对手做出类似甚至更好的产品之前，卖给大部分客户群。

We need to sell to a majority of the marketplace before the demand for this item dries up. We need to design this software so that it is easy for customers to install and learn to use. It needs to be easy to maintain and update.

我们要在这个品类的需求枯竭之前，卖给市场上的大多数人。我们要把软件设计成客户容易安装、容易学会使用。它还要容易维护、容易更新。

Many software project managers feel their job is merely to get the software completed. Without connecting the project to the business need, great software could be a failure from the organization's return on investment (ROI) point of view.

许多软件项目经理觉得自己的工作只是把软件做完。如果不把项目和业务需要连起来，从组织的投资回报（ROI）角度看，再好的软件也可能是失败。

If this is an internal project, how does this software project allow the organization to save or earn money? Will we need fewer hardware resources because what we develop is faster, more compressed, or has a better architecture? Will we be able to make more money since we can take orders faster, process them, and ship them quicker? Will we save money by creating software that needs fewer people to maintain it, or roll out an infrastructure change that lowers the number of help desk calls?

如果是内部项目，这个软件项目怎么帮组织省钱或赚钱？是因为我们开发的东西更快、更紧凑、架构更好，从而需要更少的硬件资源？还是因为我们能更快接单、处理、发货，从而赚更多钱？还是通过造一个需要更少人维护的软件、或推一项减少客服电话的基础设施变更来省钱？

— p.62 —

If our software projects are for an industry-specific systems integrator, will the way we sequence tasks or level resources increase the profit margin to the company or buy us customer goodwill with a reputation for reliability? Will our project prowess ensure that we complete more projects faster and, thus, move us to a category with our suppliers in which we get a larger discount for hardware?

如果我们的软件项目是为某个行业的系统集成商做的，我们排任务、平衡资源的方式，会提高公司利润率，还是靠可靠的口碑赢得客户好感？我们的项目实力能否保证我们更快完成更多项目，从而在供应商那里升到一个能拿到更大硬件折扣的级别？

Motivating teams and making difficult decisions on the spot become easier when we understand specifically how the completion of this project is intended to benefit the company. When making the decision to fund this particular project over all of those that were in contention, why was this one more important than those that were tabled for later?

当我们清楚地知道这个项目完成后打算怎样让公司受益时，激励团队、当场做艰难决策都会变得更容易。当初决定给这个项目拨款、而不是其他那些竞争项目时，为什么它比那些被搁置以后再议的项目更重要？

Usually the project manager is not given the answer to these critical questions, so you must learn to ask. The answer can alert you to whether time, money, or quality is the key driver on the project. When you know the answer, you can prepare workarounds, alternate solutions, and know where to spend your contingency reserves to keep your project aligned with the business reason for which it was created.

通常项目经理不会被告知这些关键问题的答案，所以你必须学会主动问。答案能告诉你：进度、成本、质量，哪个才是项目的关键驱动因素。知道答案后，你就能准备变通方案、备选解法，也知道该把应急储备花在哪里，才能让项目始终对齐它被创造出来的业务理由。

— p.63 —

Don't Skip Vacations for the Project别为了项目不度假

Joe Zenevitch · New York, New York, U.S.Joe Zenevitch · 美国纽约州纽约市

SOFTWARE PROJECT MANAGEMENT is a demanding profession. Besides being the most visible position on the team, usually you are the only one in that role and you don't have a backup. Planning time off is difficult, especially if you're a third-party consultant. You feel that your absences impact the project unfavorably.

软件项目管理是个高强度的职业。你不仅是团队里最显眼的岗位，而且通常这个角色只有你一个人，没有备份。安排休假很难，尤其是当你是第三方顾问时。你觉得自己一不在，项目就会受负面影响。

To minimize this risk, novice project managers cancel their vacations, or in the worst cases, do not plan vacations at all. I've learned over time that you really need to take periodic vacations to get a break from the stressful conditions that are inherent in most projects. Over the course of your career, how bitterly do you resent the vacations you missed? But how foggy is your memory of the specific issues you sidestepped by remaining on the job?

为了把这种风险降到最低，新手项目经理会取消假期，最糟的干脆不计划任何假期。我多年下来明白：你真的需要定期休假，从大多数项目与生俱来的高压环境中喘口气。回顾职业生涯，你对错过的假期有多耿耿于怀？可你对那些因为坚守岗位而"躲开"的具体问题，记忆又有多模糊？

I'm not suggesting that you should plan your next vacation with no regard for your project or project schedule. If it's only a three-week-duration project, you can wait. Taking a vacation the week before a major release would definitely be irresponsible. But, if your 9- to 12-month project tanks because you take a week or two off in the middle, then you are probably not managing it well in the first place.

我不是让你不管项目、不管进度，随便安排下一次休假。如果项目只有三周，你可以等等。在大版本发布前一周去度假，肯定是不负责任。但如果一个 9 到 12 个月的项目，就因为你中间离开一两周就垮了，那你一开始大概就没管好它。

Obviously, it is important to find and train someone to fill your role while you are away. He/she may not do things exactly as you would have done them, but your surrogate will be able to keep the project ship afloat and sailing in the right direction. You can make it known if you'd prefer to have major issues deferred until your return.

显然，重要的是找个人、培训他，在你不在时顶替你的角色。他/她做事可能和你不完全一样，但你的代理人能让项目这艘船浮着、朝着正确方向航行。你可以提前说清楚：重大问题最好等你回来再处理。

— p.64 —

Your replacement could be a project manager from another team, but someone from your own team is probably the better choice. A team member will be more familiar with the project, and this gives him/her a tryout run serving in a leadership role. In some organizations, the business analyst can be a good fit as an interim "you." This person knows the requirements intimately, and should know the basic mechanics of how to run your development iterations if you've been involving the stakeholders at-large all along, as you should.

顶替你的人可以是另一个团队的项目经理，但你自己团队里的人大概是更好的选择。团队成员更熟悉项目，这也让他/她有机会试一下领导角色。在有些组织里，业务分析师可以很好地临时代你。这个人对需求了如指掌；如果你一直像应该做的那样让广大相关方参与，他/她也该懂得怎么跑开发迭代的基本套路。

In agile development, the concept of the self-directed team is both important and powerful. The idea is that the project manager puts in place easy-to-understand and highly visible processes that the entire team follows. Over time, as the team adopts these processes, the project manager does less and less managing, and more and more facilitating. Essentially, removing obstacles and resolving issues replaces day-to-day micromanaging.

在敏捷开发中，自组织团队的概念既重要又强大。思路是：项目经理建立简单易懂、高度透明的流程，让整个团队遵循。久而久之，随着团队接纳这些流程，项目经理管得越来越少， facilitation（促进）做得越来越多。本质上，清除障碍、解决问题取代了日常的微观管理。

One of the delightful byproducts of a smoothly running, self-directed team is that the project manager's appropriately timed vacation can become almost a nonevent. Even if you are not around for a few days, the machine keeps running itself.

一个运转顺畅、自组织团队的可喜副产品是：项目经理在合适时机休个假，几乎不会引起任何波澜。哪怕你几天不在，这台机器也照样自己转。

Certainly schedule your vacations to make sure you are available for project releases, but definitely take time off. And never cancel a vacation just because you think the project will grind to a halt without you.

当然，安排休假时要避开项目发布节点，但一定要休假。永远不要仅仅因为觉得"没有你项目就转不动"就取消假期。

— p.65 —

Provide Regular Time to Focus留出整块专注时间

James Leigh · Toronto, Ontario, CanadaJames Leigh · 加拿安大略省多伦多

SOFTWARE DEVELOPERS REGULARLY REPORT that interruptions such as meetings, demos, and urgent bug fixes keep them from completing their work. Typically, a person takes about 20 minutes to regain his train of thought after one of these interruptions. A 5-minute question actually costs 25 minutes, and a quick 10-minute meeting actually costs 30 minutes of potential work. Interruptions and recovery time consume 28% of a typical knowledge worker's day and can cause undue frustration and stress.

软件开发人员经常反映：会议、演示、紧急修 bug 这类打断，让他们完不成活。一般来说，一个人在被打断后，要花大约 20 分钟才能重新找回思路。一个 5 分钟的问题，实际花掉 25 分钟；一个 10 分钟的短会，实际耗掉 30 分钟的潜在工作时间。打断和恢复时间，占了典型知识工作者一天的 28%，还会造成不必要的挫败和压力。

To help address this issue, set aside two hours a day (for example, between 10:00 a.m. and noon) that are interruption free. Alternately, you may be able to plan an entire day when no meetings, questions, email, phones, and other distractions are permitted, to allow developers to concentrate and focus on their work. Intel and IBM set aside Fridays, calling them "zero-email Fridays" and "Think Fridays," respectively.

为缓解这个问题，每天留出两小时（比如上午 10 点到中午）作为无打断时段。或者，你可以规划一整天，不允许开会、提问、邮件、电话和其他干扰，让开发人员专心工作。英特尔和 IBM 都把周五留出来，分别叫做"零邮件周五"和"思考周五"。

It is equally important that developers know what their top two priorities are so they can plan their work for this period effectively. Even the best-intentioned developers could only randomly guess at what these are if they're not explicitly told what will bring real business value to the project.

同样重要的是，开发人员要清楚自己最优先的两件事是什么，这样才能有效规划这段时间的工作。如果不明确告诉他们什么能给项目带来真正的业务价值，即使是最善意的开发也只能瞎猜。

Infomania (a debilitating state of information overload) is widely recognized as a major opponent to a developer's productivity. Programming requires that developers keep many things in their heads at once—everything from variables, class structures, APIs (application programming interfaces), utility methods, and even directory hierarchies. When a developer is interrupted, much of this information is "swapped out," and it requires considerable mental energy to regain it. This has a huge impact on productivity, and studies find that employees are not creating new ideas to the extent they used to because of infomania.

信息癖（信息过载导致的虚弱状态）被公认为开发人员生产力的大敌。编程要求开发同时在脑子里装很多东西——变量、类结构、API（应用编程接口）、工具方法，甚至目录层次。开发一旦被打断，这些信息大量被"换出"，要重新找回来需要大量心力。这对生产力影响巨大；研究发现，因为信息癖，员工产生新想法的能力已大不如前。

— p.66 —

In addition, different types of distractions have varying degrees of impact on the developer's train of thought. One might be able to get up, use the restroom, get a cup of coffee and a sandwich, or even move to a whiteboard, while keeping all of the program data still actively circulating in the brain. In fact, the movement might help him/her see a new avenue to solve a problem.

此外，不同类型的干扰对开发思路的影响程度不同。他可以起身、上厕所、拿杯咖啡和三明治，甚至走到白板前，同时让所有程序数据在脑子里继续活跃流转。事实上，动一动还可能帮他/她看到解决问题的新路径。

Planned meetings are especially problematic for programmers, as they might waste time when they know there is an upcoming item on their schedule. They think, "why get started only to be interrupted in 30 minutes?" And great ideas that come during meetings may be lost, or stale, by the time the developer gets back to his computer to capture them.

安排好的会议对程序员尤其成问题，因为他们知道日程上马上有会，就可能浪费时间。他们会想："现在开始，30 分钟后又要被打断，何必呢？"而会议中冒出来的好点子，等开发回到电脑前想记下来时，可能已经丢了，或者凉了。

Developers' productivity can also degrade by over 50% for each additional simultaneous project. Developers working on three or more projects often spend more time attending meetings to explain why they are not making any progress than getting any actual work done. When developers must contribute to multiple projects, make sure that they are guaranteed at least two full days on each project before switching to another. This will minimize the amount of time they must spend reintroducing themselves to each project.

开发每多同时做一个项目，生产力还会下降 50% 以上。同时做三个或更多项目的开发，往往花在开会解释"为什么没进展"上的时间，比真正干活的时间还多。当开发必须参与多个项目时，保证他们在切换到另一个项目之前，能在每个项目上至少完整工作两天。这样能把他们每次"重新进入项目上下文"所花的时间降到最低。

— p.67 —
